newsitem.title: USA: CFTC settles wash trading with Merrill, Mitsubishi.
newsitem.headline: CFTC settles wash trading with Merrill, Mitsubishi.

text.p: Merrill Lynch Futures Inc, Mitsubishi Corp and Country Hedging Inc settled charges of wash trading on wheat futures with the Commodity Futures Trading Commission on Tuesday, the CFTC said.
Merrill Lynch was also accused in an administrative complaint of recordkeeping violations, the agency said.
Mitsubishi agreed to pay $150,000, Merrill Lynch will pay $175,000 and Country Hedging will pay $75,000 under the settlement order, the agency said.
An employee of Country Hedging,trader Charles Soule, also agreed to pay $15,000 as part of the settlement.

"The commission's order addresses an important and difficult area that lies at the corn of the Commodity Exchange Act -- wash sales," said Geoffrey Aronow, director of enforcement at the CFTC. "The substantial sanctions here demonstrate the cnmmission's continuing commitment to attack misuse of the markets."

CFTC said Mitsubishi tried to shift futures trading profits from one reporting period to another for accounting purposes by placing simultaneous orders with its brokerage firm, Merrill Lynch, to buy and sell equal quantities of wheat futures spreads at approximately the same price.

The agency said it learned that Mitsubishi was willing to accept small net losses on the spread transactions in order to show profits in the nearby futures contract and corresponding losses in the deferred contract. Mitsubishi told its broker to price the purchase of the contract at the day's low price, and the sale of the contract at the day's high price, the CFTC said.
Merrill Lynch accepted Mitsubishi's simultaneous spread orders and gave them to Soule, a trader with Country Hedging at the Minneapolis Grain Exchange.

The agency also ordered Merrill to use a daily trade report to monitor customer accounts for unusual day trading activity. Country Hedging was ordered to employ a compliance officer to monitor procedures.
In a separate case, the agency also announced that it filed a complaint against a former Merrill Lynch floor broker and a Minnesota Grain Exchange broker.

The complaint alleged that in 1992 and 1993, Alfred Piasio, then an employee of Merrill Lynch, accepted simultaneous orders from his customer, Mitsubishi, and transmitted them to Soule on the Minnesota Grain Exchange trading floor.
Wilson, an independent floor broker, accepted a total of 11 pairs of simultaneous orders from Soule, the agency said.
A hearing will be scheduled before an administrative law judge, it added.
